- Pilot (Dec 15–Jan 15): 32 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (burstable)
- GA ramp (Feb–Mar): scale to 160 GPUs over 8 weeks
- Desired residency: Dedicated pool in us-west with data isolation

Key open items (please call out blockers):
- Infra: feasibility of reserving 160 GPUs by Jan 31 and recommended staging plan
- Finance: runway/commit model options (monthly reserved vs committed capacity) and impact on unit economics
- Sales: firming the ramp cadence and whether Acme will sign a 6–12 month commit if pricing is adjusted

On 2027-11-20 10:01, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Quick notes — from an infra sizing POV...
Replying with a pragmatic allocation and staging plan we can meet with existing capacity plus a modest procurement if we commit early:

Proposal (us-west Dedicated pool):
- Stage 0 (Pilot: Dec 15–Jan 15): reserve 40 A10G-equivalent GPUs (32 active, +8 buffer) — provision from shared-dedicated nodes, no new hardware purchases required.
- Stage 1 (Jan 16–Feb 28): scale to 88 GPUs — reassign nodes from flexible fleet and enable preemptible capacity as buffer during daytime peak.
- Stage 2 (Mar 1 target GA): 160 GPUs — requires procurement of additional 72 GPUs (or equivalent instances) with lead time ~6 weeks if ordering new hardware.

Constraints & notes:
- If Acme requires strict SLAs (99.9 latency guarantees) we can’t rely heavily on preemptible capacity; that pushes procurement earlier.
- Kernel optimization for their model (long-context chat) could reduce GPU count by ~10–15% — Karthik we should run profiling on the sample prompt set this week.

Next steps:
- Marcus to confirm procurement ETA with HW supply (by EOD Thurs)
- Karthik to run profiling on sample dataset (target: Wed)
- Laura to indicate preferred billing path so we can align commit timeline
Regards,
Marcus
Head of Infrastructure Operations

Thanks — quick clarifications from Sales/Account team (Acme):
- 95th pct latency SLO: 150ms for GA; during pilot latency target is more flexible (up to 300ms).
- Request mix for GA: ~70% chat inference (long context), 20% embeddings, 10% rerank/batch. Pilot will be heavier on chat (approx 80%).
- Commercial: Acme wants to know discounted unit pricing for a 6-month reserved commit vs month-to-month billing. They are willing to sign a 6-month commit if hardware placement is guaranteed; prefer a 12-month pricing schedule if we can make it attractive.

Action from our side: confirm what commitment tiers we can offer (Laura), and whether procurement lead time can be accelerated if we agree to a larger upfront commit.
